```{r setup}
res <- file.path(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)), "results")
fits <- read.csv(file.path(res, "fits.csv"))
summ <- read.csv(file.path(res, "summary.csv"))
prof <- read.csv(file.path(res, "profile.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
names(prof)[4] <- "tape_ops"
raw1 <- readRDS(dir(file.path(res, "raw"), full.names = TRUE)[1])
starts <- readRDS(file.path(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)), "..", "nlminb-r46",
                            "results", "starts.rds"))
case_lab <- c(opaka = "Opakapaka", io_yft = "IO yellowfin (AGE-SF)")
f1 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 1)
f2 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2)
jit <- fits[fits$start_id > 0, ]
s <- function(cs, m, col) summ[summ$case == cs & summ$method == m, col]
mle <- tapply(fits$mle_objective, fits$case, `[`, 1)
best_any <- tapply(jit$objective, paste(jit$case, jit$start_id), min, na.rm = TRUE)
io_best <- best_any[grepl("^io_yft", names(best_any))]
n_io_at_mle <- sum(io_best - mle[["io_yft"]] < 1e-3)
```

## Question

Can opal fits be made faster by changing the optimiser or its settings, and
where does a gradient call spend its time? This follows the comparison of
`nlminb()` in R 4.5.2 and R 4.6.2 (`benchmarks/nlminb-r46`), and uses the same
models and jittered starts.

## Setup

* `r raw1$r_version`, nloptr `r raw1$nloptr` (bundled NLopt), on one cloud
  container (4 cores; OpenMP and BLAS threads set to 1). Each case and method
  ran in a fresh R process, one at a time.
* Models: the Opakapaka quickstart fit (`r starts$opaka$n_par` parameters) and
  the IO yellowfin article model AGE-SF (`r starts$io_yft$n_par` parameters),
  rebuilt from the fits stored in opal's `inst/extdata` with the stored bounds.
* Starts: start 0 is the stored model's start;
  `r nrow(starts$opaka$starts)` (Opakapaka) and
  `r nrow(starts$io_yft$starts)` (IO yellowfin) starts are jittered around the
  stored estimate as in SS3 (jitter fraction 0.1). Tables use the jittered
  starts only.
* Timing: median of 3 repeats per start for Opakapaka; one run per start for
  IO yellowfin. Every method calls the same counted `fn`/`gr`/`he` wrappers,
  so the counts include all work, including line searches and Newton steps.
* "Reached best" means the final objective is within 1e-4 of the lowest
  objective any method reached from that start. "Reached stored" means within
  1e-3 of the stored estimate's objective or lower.

| Method | Details |
|---|---|
| nlminb, 2 passes | opal's default: `nlminb` restarted once from its own end point; `eval.max = iter.max = 10000` |
| nlminb, 1 pass | as above, without the restart |
| nlminb, 1 pass + Newton | then up to 3 Newton steps with the analytic Hessian, each kept only if inside the bounds and the objective decreases |
| nlminb with Hessian | `nlminb` given the analytic Hessian (`obj$he`); Opakapaka only (one IO yellowfin Hessian takes about 18 s) |
| nlminb, `rel.tol = 1e-8` | 2 passes with a looser relative tolerance than the default 1e-10 |
| nlminb, atomic tape | 2 passes with the model taped under `RTMB::TapeConfig(atomic = "enable")` |
| optim L-BFGS-B | `maxit = 10000` |
| optim L-BFGS-B, guarded | non-finite objective returned as 1e10, non-finite gradient elements as 0 |
| nloptr LBFGS / truncated Newton | `NLOPT_LD_LBFGS`, `NLOPT_LD_TNEWTON_PRECOND_RESTART`; `ftol_rel = 1e-10`, `maxeval = 20000` |

## Results

```{r summary-table, results = "asis"}
for (cs in c("opaka", "io_yft")) {
  d <- summ[summ$case == cs, ]
  tab <- data.frame(Method = d$label, Errors = d$errors,
                    `Reported converged` = d$reported_converged,
                    `Reached best` = d$reached_best, `Reached stored` = d$reached_mle,
                    `Median time (s)` = d$median_time_s, `Total time (s)` = d$total_time_s,
                    `Median gr calls` = d$median_gr, `Hessians` = d$total_he,
                    `Median max abs gradient` = ifelse(is.na(d$median_max_grad), "", format(signif(d$median_max_grad, 2))),
                    check.names = FALSE)
  print(knitr::kable(tab, digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 1, 0, 0, 2), row.names = FALSE,
                     caption = sprintf("%s: %d jittered starts, ordered by total time. Median time, calls and gradient exclude errors.",
                                       case_lab[cs], d$starts[1])))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

```{r fig-time, fig.height = 4.5, fig.cap = "Time per fit for each jittered start (log scale). Filled: reached the best objective from that start; open: did not. Plain L-BFGS-B is left out (it stopped with an error on most starts)."}
ord <- c("nlminb2", "nlminb1", "nlminb2_reltol8", "nlminb2_atomic", "nlminb1_newton",
         "nlminb_hessian", "lbfgsb_guard", "nloptr_lbfgs", "nloptr_tnewton")
short <- c(nlminb2 = "nlminb x2", nlminb1 = "nlminb x1", nlminb2_reltol8 = "rel.tol 1e-8",
           nlminb2_atomic = "atomic tape", nlminb1_newton = "x1 + Newton",
           nlminb_hessian = "with Hessian", lbfgsb_guard = "L-BFGS-B guarded",
           nloptr_lbfgs = "nloptr LBFGS", nloptr_tnewton = "nloptr TNewton")
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 8.5, 2, 1))
for (cs in c("opaka", "io_yft")) {
  d <- jit[jit$case == cs & jit$method %in% ord & !grepl("^error", jit$message), ]
  m <- rev(ord[ord %in% d$method])
  y <- match(d$method, m) + runif(nrow(d), -0.2, 0.2)
  plot(d$elapsed_s, y, log = "x", yaxt = "n", pch = ifelse(d$reached_best, 19, 1),
       xlab = "Time (s)", ylab = "", main = case_lab[cs], cex.main = 0.9, cex = 0.8)
  axis(2, at = seq_along(m), labels = short[m], las = 1, cex.axis = 0.8)
  abline(h = seq_along(m) + 0.5, col = "grey90")
}
par(op)
```

```{r fig-obj, fig.height = 3.8, fig.cap = "IO yellowfin: final objective minus the stored estimate's objective for each jittered start and method (log scale; values at or below 0.01 are drawn at 0.01). The grey line marks the best any method reached from that start."}
d <- jit[jit$case == "io_yft" & !grepl("^error", jit$message), ]
dd <- pmax(d$objective - d$mle_objective, 0.01)
op <- par(mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1))
plot(d$start_id + runif(nrow(d), -0.25, 0.25), dd, log = "y", pch = 1, cex = 0.8,
     xlab = "Start", ylab = "Objective - stored", xaxt = "n")
axis(1, at = 1:10)
bb <- pmax(io_best[paste("io_yft", 1:10)] - mle[["io_yft"]], 0.01)
segments(1:10 - 0.35, bb, 1:10 + 0.35, bb, col = "grey50", lwd = 2)
par(op)
```

* Opakapaka has two minima within the bounds,
  `r f2(min(jit$objective[jit$case == "opaka"], na.rm = TRUE))` and the stored
  estimate's `r f2(mle[["opaka"]])`. The `nlminb` variants reached the lower
  one from 9 or 10 of 20 starts; nloptr LBFGS reached it from `r s("opaka", "nloptr_lbfgs", "reached_best")`.
  `nlminb` with the Hessian
  ended above the stored objective from
  `r 20 - s("opaka", "nlminb_hessian", "reached_mle")` starts.
* For IO yellowfin, no method reached the stored estimate's objective from
  more than `r max(summ$reached_mle[summ$case == "io_yft"])` of 10 jittered
  starts, and the best of all methods reached it from `r n_io_at_mle`. From
  the other starts every method stopped above it, many by more than 100
  objective units. Start 5 ended in `nlminb`'s "false convergence" with every
  `nlminb` variant.
* Plain L-BFGS-B stopped with "L-BFGS-B needs finite values of 'fn'" on
  `r s("opaka", "lbfgsb", "errors")` of 20 Opakapaka and
  `r s("io_yft", "lbfgsb", "errors")` of 10 IO yellowfin starts: its line
  search steps into regions where the model returns `NaN`, which `nlminb`
  handles by shortening the step.

## Gradient cost

`opal_model()` was cut after each stage, and each cut returned the sum of
every quantity computed so far, so its tape holds all stages up to the cut.
The table gives the cost at each cut at the stored estimate; the increase from
one row to the next is the cost of that stage.

```{r profile-table, results = "asis"}
for (cs in c("opaka", "io_yft")) {
  a <- prof[prof$case == cs & prof$tape == "default", ]
  b <- prof[prof$case == cs & prof$tape == "atomic", ]
  a <- a[order(a$order), ]; b <- b[match(a$cut, b$cut), ]
  tab <- data.frame(`Cut after` = gsub("_", " ", a$cut),
                    `Tape ops` = a$tape_ops, `fn (ms)` = a$fn_ms, `gr (ms)` = a$gr_ms,
                    `Tape ops, atomic` = b$tape_ops, `fn (ms), atomic` = b$fn_ms,
                    `gr (ms), atomic` = b$gr_ms, check.names = FALSE)
  print(knitr::kable(tab, digits = c(0, 0, 2, 2, 0, 2, 2), row.names = FALSE,
                     format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
                     caption = sprintf("%s: cumulative cost at each cut, default and atomic tape. Times are medians of 5 blocks of %d calls.",
                                       case_lab[cs], if (cs == "opaka") 200L else 20L)))
  cat("\n\n")
}
p <- function(cs, cut, col, tape = "default")
  prof[prof$case == cs & prof$cut == cut & prof$tape == tape, col]
```

* IO yellowfin: the gradient costs `r f1(p("io_yft", "selectivity", "gr_ms"))` ms
  up to selectivity, `r f1(p("io_yft", "dynamics", "gr_ms"))` ms up to the
  population dynamics and `r f1(p("io_yft", "length_comp_likelihood", "gr_ms"))` ms
  once the length composition likelihood is added. The length compositions
  account for about
  `r round(100 * (p("io_yft", "length_comp_likelihood", "gr_ms") - p("io_yft", "cpue_likelihood", "gr_ms")) / p("io_yft", "length_comp_likelihood", "gr_ms"))`%
  of the gradient at that cut and the dynamics for most of the rest.
* Opakapaka: the dynamics and the length compositions cost about the same
  (`r f2(p("opaka", "dynamics", "gr_ms") - p("opaka", "initial_numbers", "gr_ms"))`
  and
  `r f2(p("opaka", "length_comp_likelihood", "gr_ms") - p("opaka", "cpue_likelihood", "gr_ms"))`
  ms).
* The atomic tape shrinks the length composition part most (IO yellowfin:
  `r format(p("io_yft", "length_comp_likelihood", "tape_ops") - p("io_yft", "cpue_likelihood", "tape_ops"), big.mark = ",")`
  to
  `r format(p("io_yft", "length_comp_likelihood", "tape_ops", "atomic") - p("io_yft", "cpue_likelihood", "tape_ops", "atomic"), big.mark = ",")`
  operations). For Opakapaka the full gradient halves
  (`r f2(p("opaka", "full", "gr_ms"))` to `r f2(p("opaka", "full", "gr_ms", "atomic"))` ms).
  For IO yellowfin the gradient at the length composition cut barely changes
  (`r f1(p("io_yft", "length_comp_likelihood", "gr_ms"))` to
  `r f1(p("io_yft", "length_comp_likelihood", "gr_ms", "atomic"))` ms), so there
  the cost is not proportional to the number of tape operations.
* The cuts keep quantities the full model drops (for example arrays it
  computes but does not return), so the cut tapes are larger than the full
  model's (IO yellowfin: `r format(p("io_yft", "weight_comp_likelihood", "tape_ops"), big.mark = ",")`
  operations at the last cut against
  `r format(p("io_yft", "full", "tape_ops"), big.mark = ",")` for the full
  model). Stage costs are therefore upper bounds; their order is the
  informative part.

## Interpretation

* `nlminb` with opal's settings was faster than every other optimiser tried
  (L-BFGS-B, nloptr LBFGS and truncated Newton, `nlminb` with the Hessian) on
  both models. For IO yellowfin it reached the best objective from as many
  starts as any of them. For Opakapaka, nloptr LBFGS found the lower of the
  two minima more often (`r s("opaka", "nloptr_lbfgs", "reached_best")`
  against `r s("opaka", "nlminb2", "reached_best")` of 20 starts) and took
  about `r f1(s("opaka", "nloptr_lbfgs", "total_time_s") / s("opaka", "nlminb2", "total_time_s"))`
  times as long; with two minima this reflects where each method's steps
  lead, and may not carry over to other models.
* One pass instead of two was `r round(100 * (1 - s("opaka", "nlminb1", "total_time_s") / s("opaka", "nlminb2", "total_time_s")))`% (Opakapaka) and
  `r round(100 * (1 - s("io_yft", "nlminb1", "total_time_s") / s("io_yft", "nlminb2", "total_time_s")))`% (IO yellowfin)
  faster in total, reached the best objective from the same number of starts,
  and left a larger final gradient (median
  `r signif(s("io_yft", "nlminb1", "median_max_grad"), 2)` against
  `r signif(s("io_yft", "nlminb2", "median_max_grad"), 2)` for IO yellowfin).
  Whether that gradient is acceptable depends on what the fit is used for.
* A looser `rel.tol` (1e-8) made no consistent difference: about 12% less
  total time for Opakapaka, about 11% more for IO yellowfin.
* Newton steps after `nlminb` bring the gradient to 1e-7 or below, at the cost
  of one Hessian per step: about `r f1(s("io_yft", "nlminb1_newton", "median_time_s") - s("io_yft", "nlminb1", "median_time_s"))` s per IO yellowfin fit.
* The atomic tape halves the Opakapaka fit time with the same end points. For
  IO yellowfin it saves little per gradient call; three starts ended at
  different points than with the default tape, in both directions, so a
  timing or quality difference cannot be separated from the start sensitivity
  below.
* For IO yellowfin, the start matters more than the optimiser:
  `r 10 - n_io_at_mle` of 10 jittered starts end above the stored estimate's objective whichever method
  is used. Faster fits from such starts do not help; more starts, or starts
  closer to the estimate, would.
* To make the IO yellowfin gradient cheaper, the length composition
  likelihood and the dynamics are where the time goes. This note does not
  identify which operations within them are costly; that needs a profile
  inside those functions.

## Limitations

* Two models, `r nrow(starts$opaka$starts)` and `r nrow(starts$io_yft$starts)`
  jittered starts, one machine. IO yellowfin timings are single runs, so
  differences of about 10% between `nlminb` variants are within run-to-run
  noise.
* The jittered starts are drawn around the stored estimate. Fits from a model's
  own initial values (as in a first fit) are further from the optimum and were
  not tested.
* Each optimiser was run with one set of settings. Other settings (for example
  L-BFGS-B's memory or tolerances, nloptr's stopping rules) could change its
  ranking.
* "Reached best" compares methods with each other. For IO yellowfin the best
  any method reached from a start is often well above the stored objective,
  so it is not evidence of a global minimum.
* The gradient profile measures cumulative cuts of `opal_model()` at one
  parameter vector; see the caveat above on cut tapes.

## Reproduce

```bash
# needs the R 4.6.2 library from benchmarks/nlminb-r46 (setup-r462.sh) with nloptr
bash benchmarks/optimizers/run-optimizers.sh
quarto render benchmarks/optimizers/optimizers.qmd
```
